You're creating a portrait data-report poster that gives developers and tech decision-makers a clear, at-a-glance understanding of which programming languages are rising and falling in 2026. Aim for a **dark-mode, developer-aesthetic** feel — think deep navy or charcoal backgrounds with vibrant accent colors (electric blue, bright green for gains, warm red/orange for losses). Typography should be clean and monospaced or semi-monospaced for data elements, paired with a modern sans-serif for headings. Keep whitespace generous; avoid clutter. The tone is authoritative and data-forward — no playful illustrations, just sharp data visualization and clean hierarchy.

The methodology note and emerging languages section should be present but visually secondary — smaller type, lower placement.

- Form, space, color, composition
- Images, graphics, shapes, patterns
- Minimal text as visual accent

- What is created: A design philosophy/aesthetic movement.

- The next phase involves making the artwork

**Name the movement** (1-2 words): "Brutalist Joy" / "Chromatic Silence" / "Metabolist Dreams"

**Articulate the philosophy** (4-6 paragraphs - concise but complete):

To capture the VISUAL essence, express how the philosophy manifests through:
- Space and form
- Color and material
- Scale and rhythm
- Composition and balance
- Visual hierarchy

Philosophy: Communication through monumental form and bold geometry.
Visual expression: Massive color blocks, sculptural typography (huge single words, tiny labels), Brutalist spatial divisions, Polish poster energy meets Le Corbusier. Ideas expressed through visual weight and spatial tension, not explanation. Text as rare, powerful gesture - never paragraphs, only essential words integrated into the visual architecture. Every element placed with the precision of a master craftsman.

**"Chromatic Language"**
Philosophy: Color as the primary information system.
Visual expression: Geometric precision where color zones create meaning. Typography minimal - small sans-serif labels letting chromatic fields communicate. Think Josef Albers' interaction meets data visualization. Information encoded spatially and chromatically. Words only to anchor what color already shows. The result of painstaking chromatic calibration.

**"Analog Meditation"**
Philosophy: Quiet visual contemplation through texture and breathing room.
Visual expression: Paper grain, ink bleeds, vast negative space. Photography and illustration dominate. Typography whispered (small, restrained, serving the visual). Japanese photobook aesthetic. Images breathe across pages. Text appears sparingly - short phrases, never explanatory blocks. Each composition balanced with the care of a meditation practice.

**"Organic Systems"**
Philosophy: Natural clustering and modular growth patterns.
Visual expression: Rounded forms, organic arrangements, color from nature through architecture. Information shown through visual diagrams, spatial relationships, iconography. Text only for key labels floating in space. The composition tells the story through expert spatial orchestration.

**"Geometric Silence"**
Philosophy: Pure order and restraint.
Visual expression: Grid-based precision, bold photography or stark graphics, dramatic negative space. Typography precise but minimal - small essential text, large quiet zones. Swiss formalism meets Brutalist material honesty. Structure communicates, not words. Every alignment the work of countless refinements.

Create something that could be shown to people to prove expertise and rank as undeniably impressive.

Rather than adding a fun filter or refactoring a font, consider how to make the existing composition more cohesive with the art. If the instinct is to call a new function or draw a new shape, STOP and instead ask: "How can I make what's already here more of a piece of art?"

Take a second pass. Go back to the code and refine/polish further to make this a philosophically designed masterpiece.

To create additional pages when requested, create more creative pages along the same lines as the design philosophy but distinctly different as well. Bundle those pages in the same .pdf or many .pngs. Treat the first page as just a single page in a whole coffee table book waiting to be filled. Make the next pages unique twists and memories of the original. Have them almost tell a story in a very tasteful way. Exercise full creative freedom."}

# PYPL Programming Language Popularity Index — April 2026

## Overview

The PYPL (PopularitY of Programming Language) Index measures how frequently programming language tutorials are searched on Google worldwide. Because it captures learning intent rather than existing web-page counts, PYPL serves as a **leading indicator** of language adoption. The raw data is sourced from Google Trends and normalized so that all language shares sum to 100%, smoothed over a six-month window.

As of April 2026, **Python commands 36.21%** of all tutorial searches globally, reinforcing its position as the dominant language for the fourth consecutive year.

## Top 10 Languages — Worldwide Rankings

| Rank | Language | Share | 1-Year Trend |
|------|------------|--------|-------------|
| 1 | Python | 36.21% | +5.7% |
| 2 | C/C++ | 13.21% | +6.2% |
| 3 | Java | 10.01% | -5.4% |
| 4 | R | 6.17% | +1.6% |
| 5 | JavaScript | 5.07% | -3.0% |
| 6 | Swift | 3.15% | +0.8% |
| 7 | C# | 3.00% | -3.0% |
| 8 | Rust | 2.98% | -0.1% |
| 9 | PHP | 2.96% | -0.7% |
| 10 | Objective-C | 2.57% | +0.1% |

Python alone accounts for more than a third of all programming tutorial searches, nearly triple the share of its closest competitor.

## Biggest Gainers and Losers

The most dramatic year-over-year movement belongs to **C/C++**, which surged **+6.2 percentage points** to claim the #2 spot at 13.21%. Python also grew strongly at +5.7%. On the declining side, **Java fell 5.4 points**, dropping to just above 10%, while **JavaScript** and **C#** each shed 3.0 points.

Over a five-year horizon, the picture is even starker: **C/C++ gained +7.0%** cumulatively, the largest long-term increase of any language, while **Java lost -7.0%**, the steepest long-term decline.

## Emerging and Noteworthy Languages

Beyond the top 10, several languages show interesting trajectories:

| Language | Share | 1-Year Trend | Note |
|----------|-------|-------------|------|
| Ada | 2.51% | +1.1% | Strong growth in safety-critical domains |
| R | 6.17% | +1.6% | Data-science demand continues |
| Julia | 0.73% | +0.4% | Steady rise in scientific computing |
| Go | 0.71% | -1.3% | Notable decline despite cloud-native popularity |
| Kotlin | 0.90% | -0.9% | Declining despite Android backing |
| Zig | 0.24% | +0.0% | Niche but stable systems language |

Rust holds steady at 2.98% (essentially flat at -0.1%), maintaining its position just outside the top 7 but not experiencing the explosive growth some predicted.

## Methodology in Brief

PYPL exports Google Trends CSV data and processes it with Python's pandas library. Each language's tutorial search interest is measured relative to Java tutorials each month, then normalized to 100%. A six-month smoothing window reduces noise. Unlike the TIOBE Index, which counts existing web pages (a lagging indicator), PYPL focuses on **search intent** — what developers are actively trying to learn — making it a forward-looking measure of language momentum.

## Key Takeaways

- **C/C++ is the breakout story of 2026**, posting the largest gains both year-over-year (+6.2%) and over five years (+7.0%).
- **Java's long slide continues**, losing 5.4 points in a single year and 7.0 points over five years.
- **JavaScript and C# are under pressure**, each dropping 3.0 points year-over-year.
- **R and Ada are quiet gainers**, reflecting sustained demand in data science and safety-critical engineering respectively.

*Data: PYPL / Google Trends, April 2026. © Pierre Carbonnelle, CC BY 3.0.*

# Terminal Noir — Design Philosophy

## Aesthetic Foundation

A dark-mode visual language that treats data as monument. Dense information rendered with the precision of a master craftsman — every percentage point, every rank number placed as deliberately as a typesetter setting lead. The aesthetic draws from the quiet authority of terminal interfaces, the rigor of engineering blueprints, and the visual weight of film noir composition. Information is not displayed; it is exhibited, like artifacts in a museum of computational history. The craftsmanship is meticulous — countless hours of refinement visible in the spacing between elements, the calibration of luminance, the exactness of alignment that only reveals itself upon sustained examination.

## Spatial Language

Space functions as both breathing room and hierarchy. Generous negative space separates the dominant Python callout from the rankings table below — not mere decoration, but intentional tension between elements. The portrait canvas rises vertically, creating a sense of ascent, of data climbing toward revelation. Sections are divided not by lines or boxes, but by shifts in luminosity — darker zones containing dense data, lighter zones offering visual rest. Every millimeter of margin is calculated; the eye moves in a deliberate path from headline metrics downward through increasingly granular data. The composition should appear as though a master spent hours adjusting a single pixel of whitespace.

## Chromatic System

The palette operates in three registers: the deep navy-charcoal ground (the silence), electric accent colors (the signal), and pure white (the truth). Navy and charcoal create a void from which data emerges luminous. Electric cyan marks the dominant Python metric — cool, authoritative, radiating calm confidence. Bright green signifies gains — urgent but not alarming, like a healthy pulse. Warm orange-red marks decline — danger without panic, a warning rendered elegant. The chromatic contrast between these registers must be painstakingly calibrated so each color pops distinctly without bleeding. Every hue choice should feel inevitable, as if the colors themselves demanded to exist in these exact proportions.

## Typography & Text

Typography is architectural — not decorative. Monospace numerals for all percentage values, creating a sense of technical precision and machine-readable authority. A clean sans-serif for headings and labels, geometric and unapologetic. Text appears sparingly, as pure visual gesture — short, powerful statements that anchor what the design already shows. The Python/C/C++/Java headline callouts are treated as visual objects, not copy blocks; their placement creates visual tension and balance. Every character of text earns its position through necessity, not habit. The typeface selection demonstrates expert-level visual judgment.

## Visual Hierarchy & Composition

The poster builds vertically from drama to detail. The three headline metrics — Python at 36.21%, C/C++ at 13.21%, Java at 10.01% — occupy the upper third with dominant scale, their proportions establishing power dynamics before the viewer reads a single word. The rankings table dominates the center, its rows creating rhythm through repetition with subtle variation in share values. Trend arrows and color-coding provide immediate visual parsing. Below, methodology and emerging languages receive secondary treatment — smaller scale, lower contrast, visually subordinate but present for credibility. The composition achieves the precision of a master-crafted artifact: nothing overlaps, nothing crowds, every element has breathing room and clear purpose. The final result should feel inevitable, as if no other arrangement were possible.

    draw_centered_text(draw, "PYTHON", metric_y + 95, f_heading, WHITE)

    side_h = 130
    gap = 40

    num_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    num_x = cpp_x + (side_w - num_w) // 2
    draw.text((num_x, y + 12), "13.21", font=f_mono_large, fill=GREEN)

    draw_centered_text(draw, "C/C++", y + 62, f_subhead, WHITE, cpp_x + side_w // 2)
    draw_centered_text(draw, "#2 +6.2%", y + 86, f_mono_sm, GREEN, cpp_x + side_w // 2) + 5

    draw.rounded_rectangle([java_x, y, java_x + side_w, y + side_h], radius=10, fill=BG_MID)

    draw_centered_text(draw, "#3  -5.4%", y + 86, f_mono_sm, RED, java_x + side_w // 2) + 5

    y += side_h + 40

    # === KEY INSIGHT BAR ===
    insight_text = "Python dominates search share — nearly 3× its nearest competitor"
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), insight_text, font=f_small)
    text_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    draw.rounded_rectangle([(WIDTH - text_w - 60) // 2, y, (WIDTH + text_w + 60) // 2, y + 40], radius=6, fill=(25, 30, 50))
    draw_centered_text(draw, insight_text, y + 10, f_small, (150, 160, 190))

    y += 60

    # === TOP 10 RANKINGS TABLE ===
    draw_centered_text(draw, "TOP 10 LANGUAGES BY SEARCH SHARE", y, f_heading, OFF_WHITE)
    y += 45

    # Table header

    rank_x = 80
    lang_x = 180
    share_x = 520
    trend_x = 700

    # Header background
    draw.rectangle([60, header_y, WIDTH - 60, header_y + 35], fill=(22, 27, 45))

    draw.text((rank_x, header_y + 6), "RANK", font=f_mono_xs, fill=(120, 130, 160))
    draw.text((lang_x, header_y + 6), "LANGUAGE", font=f_mono_xs, fill=(120, 130, 160))
    draw.text((share_x, header_y + 6), "SHARE", font=f_mono_xs, fill=(120, 130, 160))
    draw.text((trend_x, header_y + 6), "1-YR", font=f_mono_xs, fill=(120, 130, 160))

    y = header_y + 40

    # Table data
    rankings = [
        (1, "Python", "36.21%", "+5.7%", CYAN, GREEN),
        (2, "C/C++", "13.21%", "+6.2%", GREEN, GREEN),
        (3, "Java", "10.01%", "-5.4%", RED, RED),
        (4, "R", "6.17%", "+1.6%", WHITE, GREEN),
        (5, "JavaScript", "5.07%", "-3.0%", WHITE, RED),
        (6, "Swift", "3.15%", "+0.8%", WHITE, GREEN),
        (7, "C#", "3.00%", "-3.0%", WHITE, RED),
        (8, "Rust", "2.98%", "-0.1%", WHITE, OFF_WHITE),
        (9, "PHP", "2.96%", "-0.7%", WHITE, RED),
        (10, "Objective-C", "2.57%", "+0.1%", WHITE, GREEN),
    ]

    for rank, lang, share, trend, lang_color, trend_color in rankings:
        # Row background (alternating)
        if rank % 2 == 1:
            draw.rectangle([60, y - 2, WIDTH - 60, y + 30], fill=(16, 20, 35))

        # Rank
        draw.text((rank_x, y), f"{rank:2d}", font=f_mono_sm, fill=(100, 110, 140))

        # Language
        draw.text((lang_x, y), lang, font=f_mono_sm, fill=lang_color)

        # Share
        bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), share, font=f_mono_sm)
        share_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
        draw.text((share_x + 50 - share_w, y), share, font=f_mono_sm, fill=WHITE)

        # Trend
        arrow = "▲" if trend.startswith("+") else "▼" if trend.startswith("-") else ""
        trend_display = f"{arrow} {trend}"
        bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), trend_display, font=f_mono_sm)
        trend_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
        draw.text((trend_x + 60 - trend_w, y), trend_display, font=f_mono_sm, fill=trend_color)

        y += 36

    # === BIGGEST MOVERS SECTION ===

    y += 45

    movers = [
        ("C/C++", "+6.2%", "Largest 1-year gain", GREEN),
        ("Python", "+5.7%", "Strong growth", GREEN),
        ("Java", "-5.4%", "Largest 1-year decline", RED),
        ("JavaScript", "-3.0%", "Significant drop", RED),
        ("C#", "-3.0%", "Under pressure", RED),
    ]

    # Create movers grid
    mover_w = 180
    mover_h = 90
    mover_gap = 30
    start_x = (WIDTH - 3 * mover_w - 2 * mover_gap) // 2

    for i, (lang, change, note, color) in enumerate(movers):
        col = i % 3
        row = i // 3
        mx = start_x + col * (mover_w + mover_gap)
        my = y + row * (mover_h + 20)

        draw.rounded_rectangle([mx, my, mx + mover_w, my + mover_h], radius=8, fill=BG_MID)

        # Change value
        bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), change, font=f_mono_med)
        cx = mx + (mover_w - (bbox[2] - bbox[0])) // 2
        draw.text((cx, my + 12), change, font=f_mono_med, fill=color)

        # Language name
        bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), lang, font=f_body)
        lx = mx + (mover_w - (bbox[2] - bbox[0])) // 2
        draw.text((lx, my + 48), lang, font=f_body, fill=WHITE)

        # Note
        bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), note, font=f_small)
        nx = mx + (mover_w - (bbox[2] - bbox[0])) // 2
        draw.text((nx, my + 68), note, font=f_small, fill=(120, 130, 160))

    y += 3 * (mover_h + 20) + 30

    # === 5-YEAR TRENDS ===
    draw.rounded_rectangle([60, y, WIDTH - 60, y + 80], radius=10, fill=BG_MID)

    draw.text((100, y + 15), "5-YEAR SPOTLIGHT", font=f_subhead, fill=OFF_WHITE)

    draw.text((100, y + 45), "C/C++", font=f_mono_sm, fill=GREEN)
    draw.text((200, y + 45), "+7.0%", font=f_mono_sm, fill=GREEN)
    draw.text((290, y + 45), "Biggest 5-year growth", font=f_small, fill=(120, 130, 160))

    # Java loss

    draw.text((640, y + 45), "-7.0%", font=f_mono_sm, fill=RED)
    draw.text((730, y + 45), "Biggest decline", font=f_small, fill=(120, 130, 160))

    y += 100

    # === EMERGING LANGUAGES ===
    draw_centered_text(draw, "LANGUAGES TO WATCH", y, f_heading, OFF_WHITE)
    y += 40

    emerging = [
        ("Ada", "2.51%", "+1.1%", "Safety-critical domains", GREEN),
        ("R", "6.17%", "+1.6%", "Data science demand", GREEN),
        ("Julia", "0.73%", "+0.4%", "Scientific computing", GREEN),

        ("Zig", "0.24%", "+0.0%", "Niche but stable", OFF_WHITE),
    ]

    # Two columns
    col1_x = 100
    col2_x = 580
    row_h = 38

    for i, (lang, share, trend, note, color) in enumerate(emerging):
        col = i % 2
        row = i // 2
        ex = col1_x if col == 0 else col2_x
        ey = y + row * row_h

        draw.text((ex, ey), lang, font=f_mono_sm, fill=WHITE)
        draw.text((ex + 90, ey), share, font=f_mono_xs, fill=OFF_WHITE)

        arrow = "▲" if trend.startswith("+") else "▼" if trend.startswith("-") else "–"
        draw.text((ex + 170, ey), f"{arrow} {trend}", font=f_mono_xs, fill=color)

        draw.text((ex + 250, ey), note, font=f_small, fill=(100, 110, 140))

    y += 3 * row_h + 30

    # === METHODOLOGY FOOTER ===
    draw.rectangle([0, y, WIDTH, y + 2], fill=(30, 35, 55))

    y += 20
    method_text = "Methodology: PYPL analyzes Google Trends tutorial search data, normalized to sum 100%, smoothed over 6 months."
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), method_text, font=f_small)
    text_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    draw.text(((WIDTH - text_w) // 2, y), method_text, font=f_small, fill=(90, 100, 120))

    y += 28
    source_text = "Source: PYPL / Google Trends, April 2026  |  © Pierre Carbonnelle, CC BY 3.0"
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), source_text, font=f_small)
    text_w = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    draw.text(((WIDTH - text_w) // 2, y), source_text, font=f_small, fill=(80, 90, 110))

    # === DECORATIVE ELEMENTS ===
    # Top accent line
    draw.rectangle([0, 0, WIDTH, 4], fill=CYAN)

    # Bottom accent
    draw.rectangle([0, HEIGHT - 4, WIDTH, HEIGHT], fill=(20, 25, 40))

    # Save
    img.save("/app/output/final_poster.png", "PNG", quality=95)
    print("Poster saved to /app/output/final_poster.png")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os
    os.makedirs("/app/output", exist_ok=True)
    create_poster()

def text_width(text, font):
    bbox = ImageDraw.Draw(Image.new('RGB', (1, 1))).textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0]

def center_text(draw, text, y, font, color, x_center=None):
    w = text_width(text, font)
    x = (WIDTH - w) // 2 if x_center is None else x_center - w // 2
    draw.text((x, y), text, font=font, fill=color)
    bbox = draw.textbbox((x, y), text, font=font)
    return bbox[3]

    draw.rounded_rectangle([x1, y1, x2, y2], radius=radius, fill=fill)

PYPL Programming Language Popularity Index — April 2026

# Canvas dimensions (portrait)

GREEN_DIM = (0, 160, 85)        # Muted green

    except:

# Font sizes
f_display = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}JetBrainsMono-Bold.ttf", 80)   # Hero numbers
f_title = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}WorkSans-Bold.ttf", 38)
f_heading = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}WorkSans-SemiBold.ttf", 22)
f_label = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}WorkSans-Medium.ttf", 15)
f_body = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}WorkSans-Regular.ttf", 14)
f_small = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}WorkSans-Regular.ttf", 12)
f_mono_xl = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}JetBrainsMono-Bold.ttf", 56)
f_mono_lg = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}JetBrainsMono-Bold.ttf", 36)
f_mono_md = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}JetBrainsMono-Bold.ttf", 22)
f_mono_sm = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf", 16)
f_mono_xs = load_font(f"{FONT_DIR}JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf", 13)

def text_width(text, font):
    bbox = ImageDraw.Draw(Image.new('RGB', (1, 1))).textbbox((0, 0), text, font=font)
    return bbox[2] - bbox[0]

def center_text(draw, text, y, font, color, x_center=None):
    w = text_width(text, font)
    x = (WIDTH - w) // 2 if x_center is None else x_center - w // 2
    draw.text((x, y), text, font=font, fill=color)
    bbox = draw.textbbox((x, y), text, font=font)
    return bbox[3]

def draw_rounded_rect(draw, xy, radius, fill):
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = xy
    draw.rounded_rectangle([x1, y1, x2, y2], radius=radius, fill=fill)

def create_poster():
    img = Image.new('RGB', (WIDTH, HEIGHT), BG_DEEP)
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

    # === TOP ACCENT BAR ===
    draw.rectangle([0, 0, WIDTH, 5], fill=CYAN)

    y = 45

    # === HEADER ===
    center_text(draw, "PYPL INDEX", y, f_title, WHITE)
    y += 52
    center_text(draw, "Programming Language Popularity", y, f_heading, OFF_WHITE)
    y += 30
    center_text(draw, "April 2026", y, f_body, DIM_TEXT)
    y += 55

    # === HERO METRIC — PYTHON DOMINANCE ===
    # Large centered card
    card_w = 500
    card_h = 200
    card_x = (WIDTH - card_w) // 2
    draw_rounded_rect(draw, [card_x, y, card_x + card_w, y + card_h], 16, BG_DARK)

    # Hero number
    num = "36.21"
    num_x = card_x + (card_w - text_width(num, f_display)) // 2
    draw.text((num_x, y + 25), num, font=f_display, fill=CYAN)

    # Label
    center_text(draw, "P Y T H O N", y + 115, f_heading, WHITE, card_x + card_w // 2)
    center_text(draw, "#1 Worldwide — +5.7% year-over-year", y + 145, f_body, DIM_TEXT, card_x + card_w // 2)
    center_text(draw, "Tutorial search share worldwide", y + 168, f_small, (80, 90, 110), card_x + card_w // 2)

    y += card_h + 35

    # === DUAL METRICS — C/C++ AND JAVA ===
    side_w = 280
    side_h = 140
    gap = 60

    # C/C++ card (left)
    cpp_x = (WIDTH - 2 * side_w - gap) // 2
    draw_rounded_rect(draw, [cpp_x, y, cpp_x + side_w, y + side_h], 12, BG_DARK)

    num = "13.21"
    num_x = cpp_x + (side_w - text_width(num, f_mono_xl)) // 2
    draw.text((num_x, y + 15), num, font=f_mono_xl, fill=GREEN)
    center_text(draw, "C/C++", y + 75, f_heading, WHITE, cpp_x + side_w // 2)
    center_text(draw, "#2 +6.2% ▲ Largest gain", y + 100, f_mono_xs, GREEN_DIM, cpp_x + side_w // 2)

    # Java card (right)
    java_x = cpp_x + side_w + gap
    draw_rounded_rect(draw, [java_x, y, java_x + side_w, y + side_h], 12, BG_DARK)

    num = "10.01"
    num_x = java_x + (side_w - text_width(num, f_mono_xl)) // 2
    draw.text((num_x, y + 15), num, font=f_mono_xl, fill=RED)
    center_text(draw, "JAVA", y + 75, f_heading, WHITE, java_x + side_w // 2)
    center_text(draw, "#3 -5.4% ▼ Steepest decline", y + 100, f_mono_xs, RED_DIM, java_x + side_w // 2)

    y += side_h + 50

    # === SECTION: TOP 10 RANKINGS ===
    center_text(draw, "TOP 10 LANGUAGES BY SEARCH SHARE", y, f_heading, OFF_WHITE)
    y += 50

    # Table header
    header_y = y
    draw.rectangle([70, header_y, WIDTH - 70, header_y + 32], fill=BG_MID)

    col_rank = 90
    col_lang = 170
    col_share = 560
    col_trend = 720

    draw.text((col_rank, header_y + 8), "RANK", font=f_mono_xs, fill=DIM_TEXT)
    draw.text((col_lang, header_y + 8), "LANGUAGE", font=f_mono_xs, fill=DIM_TEXT)
    draw.text((col_share, header_y + 8), "SHARE", font=f_mono_xs, fill=DIM_TEXT)
    draw.text((col_trend, header_y + 8), "1-YEAR", font=f_mono_xs, fill=DIM_TEXT)

    y = header_y + 40

    # Rankings data
    rankings = [
        (1, "Python", "36.21", "+5.7", CYAN, GREEN),
        (2, "C/C++", "13.21", "+6.2", GREEN, GREEN),
        (3, "Java", "10.01", "-5.4", RED, RED),
        (4, "R", "6.17", "+1.6", OFF_WHITE, GREEN),
        (5, "JavaScript", "5.07", "-3.0", OFF_WHITE, RED),
        (6, "Swift", "3.15", "+0.8", OFF_WHITE, GREEN),
        (7, "C#", "3.00", "-3.0", OFF_WHITE, RED),
        (8, "Rust", "2.98", "-0.1", OFF_WHITE, DIM_TEXT),
        (9, "PHP", "2.96", "-0.7", OFF_WHITE, RED),
        (10, "Objective-C", "2.57", "+0.1", OFF_WHITE, GREEN),
    ]

    for idx, (rank, lang, share, trend, lang_col, trend_col) in enumerate(rankings):
        row_y = y + idx * 38

        # Alternating row background
        if idx % 2 == 0:
            draw.rectangle([70, row_y - 3, WIDTH - 70, row_y + 30], fill=(16, 19, 35))

        # Rank number
        draw.text((col_rank, row_y), f"{rank:2d}", font=f_mono_sm, fill=(90, 100, 125))

        # Language
        draw.text((col_lang, row_y), lang, font=f_mono_sm, fill=lang_col)

        # Share (right-aligned)
        share_w = text_width(share, f_mono_sm)
        draw.text((col_share + 70 - share_w, row_y), f"{share}%", font=f_mono_sm, fill=WHITE)

        # Trend with arrow
        arrow = "▲" if trend.startswith("+") else "▼" if trend.startswith("-") else "–"
        trend_text = f"{arrow} {trend}%"
        trend_w = text_width(trend_text, f_mono_sm)
        draw.text((col_trend + 80 - trend_w, row_y), trend_text, font=f_mono_sm, fill=trend_col)

    y += len(rankings) * 38 + 45

    # === BIGGEST MOVERS GRID ===
    center_text(draw, "BIGGEST MOVERS", y, f_heading, OFF_WHITE)
    y += 48

    movers = [
        ("C/C++", "+6.2", "Largest 1-year gain", GREEN),
        ("Python", "+5.7", "Strong growth", GREEN),
        ("Java", "-5.4", "Largest decline", RED),
        ("JavaScript", "-3.0", "Under pressure", RED),
        ("C#", "-3.0", "Losing momentum", RED),
    ]

    mover_w = 186
    mover_h = 95

    for i, (lang, change, note, color) in enumerate(movers):

        mx = start_x + col * (mover_w + gap_x)

        draw_rounded_rect(draw, [mx, my, mx + mover_w, my + mover_h], 10, BG_DARK)

        # Change

        chg_x = mx + (mover_w - text_width(chg_text, f_mono_md)) // 2
        draw.text((chg_x, my + 15), chg_text, font=f_mono_md, fill=color)

        # Language
        lbl_x = mx + (mover_w - text_width(lang, f_label)) // 2
        draw.text((lbl_x, my + 48), lang, font=f_label, fill=WHITE)

        # Note
        note_x = mx + (mover_w - text_width(note, f_small)) // 2
        draw.text((note_x, my + 70), note, font=f_small, fill=DIM_TEXT)

    y += 3 * (mover_h + gap_y) + 35

    # === 5-YEAR SPOTLIGHT BAR ===
    draw_rounded_rect(draw, [60, y, WIDTH - 60, y + 75], 12, BG_MID)

    center_text(draw, "5-YEAR TREND SPOTLIGHT", y + 12, f_label, DIM_TEXT)

    # C/C++ gain indicator
    draw.text((110, y + 38), "C/C++", font=f_mono_sm, fill=GREEN)
    draw.text((200, y + 38), "+7.0%", font=f_mono_md, fill=GREEN)
    draw.text((300, y + 40), "Biggest 5-year growth among all languages", font=f_small, fill=DIM_TEXT)

    # Java loss indicator
    draw.text((580, y + 38), "Java", font=f_mono_sm, fill=RED)
    draw.text((660, y + 38), "-7.0%", font=f_mono_md, fill=RED)
    draw.text((760, y + 40), "Steepest 5-year decline", font=f_small, fill=DIM_TEXT)

    y += 95

    # === EMERGING LANGUAGES ===
    center_text(draw, "LANGUAGES TO WATCH", y, f_heading, OFF_WHITE)
    y += 45

    emerging = [
        ("Ada", "2.51%", "+1.1", "Safety-critical systems", GREEN),
        ("R", "6.17%", "+1.6", "Data science demand", GREEN),
        ("Julia", "0.73%", "+0.4", "Scientific computing", GREEN),
        ("Go", "0.71%", "-1.3", "Cloud-native decline", RED),
        ("Kotlin", "0.90%", "-0.9", "Android fading", RED),
        ("Zig", "0.24%", "+0.0", "Niche stable", DIM_TEXT),
    ]

    col1_x = 100
    col2_x = 570
    row_h = 36

    for i, (lang, share, trend, note, color) in enumerate(emerging):
        col = i % 2
        ex = col1_x if col == 0 else col2_x
        ey = y + (i // 2) * row_h

        # Language name
        draw.text((ex, ey), lang, font=f_mono_sm, fill=WHITE)

        # Share
        draw.text((ex + 95, ey), share, font=f_mono_xs, fill=DIM_TEXT)

        # Trend
        arrow = "▲" if trend.startswith("+") and trend != "+0.0" else "▼" if trend.startswith("-") else "–"
        trend_disp = f"{arrow} {trend}%"
        draw.text((ex + 175, ey), trend_disp, font=f_mono_xs, fill=color)

        # Note
        draw.text((ex + 275, ey), note, font=f_small, fill=(85, 95, 115))

    y += 3 * row_h + 40

    # === FOOTER ===
    draw.rectangle([0, y, WIDTH, y + 1], fill=(35, 40, 60))
    y += 18

    method = "Methodology: PYPL analyzes Google Trends tutorial search data — normalized to 100%, 6-month smoothing. Captures learning intent, not web presence."
    draw.text(((WIDTH - text_width(method, f_small)) // 2, y), method, font=f_small, fill=(75, 85, 100))

    y += 25
    source = "Source: PYPL / Google Trends, April 2026  |  © Pierre Carbonnelle, CC BY 3.0"
    draw.text(((WIDTH - text_width(source, f_small)) // 2, y), source, font=f_small, fill=(60, 70, 85))

    # Bottom accent
    draw.rectangle([0, HEIGHT - 6, WIDTH, HEIGHT], fill=BG_DARK)

    # Save
    img.save("/app/output/final_poster.png", "PNG")
    print("Masterpiece poster saved to /app/output/final_poster.png")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import os
    os.makedirs("/app/output", exist_ok=True)
    create_poster()
